name: Counting the Occurrences of One String in Another (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that has a function that receives a string and returns the number of times that the string "hi" appears anywhere in the given string, ignoring the case.
code:
#Step 1: Define the function
def count_hi(s):
    #Step 1.1: Assign initial value to the variable that we need for the counts
    count = 0
    #Step 1.2: Iterate through the characters in the given string 
    for i in range(len(s)-1):
        #Step 1.2.1: Increment the counts by 1 if we find a match
        if s[i:i+2].lower() == "hi":
            count += 1
    #Step 1.3: Return the counts
    return count
#Step 2: Call the function
print(count_hi("hiabc Hi ho hIx"))

commentList:
We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function count_hi that receives a string and returns the number of times that the string "hi" appears anywhere in the given string, ignoring the case. The given string is referred by variable s.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.

3.content: #Step 1.1: Assign initial value to the variable that we need for the counts

commentList: We need this variable to count the occurrences of the string "hi" in the given string. Of course, it should be initialized with 0 because we have not started counting yet.

5.content: #Step 1.2: Iterate through the characters in the given string

commentList: We need to search for a match by checking if each two adjacent characters in the given string are equal to the string "hi". We can achieve this by iterating over the indexes of the characters in the given string and then checking the substring that begins at each index and extends to the character at the immediate next index. We need the indexes of the string characters to start at 0 (index of the first character) with every integer number up to but not including the len(s)-1. We get this sequence by calling the range(len(s)-1) function.
The reason that we do not include the index of the last character in the sequence is that we check the character at the last index when we get to the second last index of the given string.
Note that len(s) returns the number of the characters in the string. Also note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

7.content: #Step 1.2.1: Increment the counts by 1 if we find a match

commentList:
We need to compare the string "hi" with the substring that begins at the index i and extends to the character at index i+1. If this substring is equal to string "hi" (ignoring the case), then we increment the number of occurrences of the string "hi" in the given string by 1.

s[i:i+2] fetches a range of characters starting from the index i and ending with the character at the index i+1 of the given string.

Note that we could compare two strings using == operator. Also, the function lower() returns a copy of the string in which all case-based characters have been lowercased. We need to call this function because we want a case-insensitive string comparison.

If the substring that begins at the index i and extends to the character at index i+1 is equal to the string "hi" (ignoring the case), then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
When we find a match starting at the character at the index i of the given string, then we have to increment the number of occurrences of the string "hi" in the given string by 1.
The += operator adds 1 to the value of variable count and the result is stored into the variable count. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement count = count + 1.
This statement returns the  number of occurrences of the string "hi" in the given string.
The return statement, when reached, ends the function call and sends the result back to the caller.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the value returned from the function call. Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from the function call in a variable. We could use the value returned from the function call directly in the print function.
Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared.
